contractRequests: WP-39 (canonical) and the spec owner: 02 req 19 says a JSON null in the hub is an internal error, and 02 req 24 says null is never emitted. That cannot hold for free content. Inside open configs, plugin configs, Plugin configSchema and the JSONSchemaDocument value, null is valid data: draft 2020-12 `const: null`, `enum: [null]` and `default: null` all pass stage F. Stage G keeps these nulls. The canonical encoder must emit null at free positions; 'null never emitted' should be read as 'never at a schema-typed position'.

WP-69 (pipeline) and WP-39: the R-64 exemption is read from the file table. Stage G skips the range rule for a resource when files.File(res.Start.File).Role == tree.RoleCanonical. Canonical.Decode output re-entering through FromResources therefore needs a Start position in a file registered with RoleCanonical, and the pipeline must pass that FileTable to defaults.Stage.Run or Stage.Resource. Without it the content counts as authored and the range rule applies. The same rule makes hub.Source.File empty for canonical content.

WP-28 or WP-29 (schema or configuration model): add a schema marker or a configuration-model sentence for host-name fields, so host-case normalization (Route spec.match.hosts, Gateway spec.listeners[].hostnames, ASCII lower case) no longer needs stage G to identify those fields by $defs name (RouteMatch.hosts, Listener.hostnames).

Stage F (internal/config/schemaview, WP-35) and docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md (with spec 02 req 19): state that JSON null is rejected in free content too, meaning undeclared members of +ruralz:open configs, plugin configs, Plugin spec.configSchema and the validation.json-schema config.schema (JSONSchemaDocument). Stage G now reports it as RZ-CFG-005 at the null's key-aware path. State that inline JSON Schema documents cannot use null literals in M1 (for example "enum": [null], "const": null, "default": null), or define a canonical representation for them. Stage F could report this first, so the CLI shows it alongside the other schema findings.

Pipeline (WP-69, internal/config/pipeline): Stage.Run now enforces the 01 req 50 cap within stage G. It returns at most defaults.MaxDiagnostics diagnostics plus one RZ-CFG-001 with the same message as diag.Collector. The pipeline should add this list to its run-wide Collector and stop once the result holds RZ-CFG-001 or Collector.Full(). If the 10,000 cap must cover all stages together rather than each stage, Run needs a remaining-budget argument (for example an Options field or an extra parameter). That would be an additive change for this package.

pkg/config/v1alpha1 JSONSchemaDocument.UnmarshalJSON runs json.Valid over the whole inline schema in one call, which no worker can yield inside (01 req 53). About 1 ms for a 500 KB document. If 100 µs must hold for inline schemas too, that check needs a validator that can be stopped part-way, or should move to stage F, which already validates the document.
deviations: Host-case normalization comes from the WP-37 scope ('host case'), not from a numbered requirement. It lower-cases only the ASCII letters of Route spec.match.hosts and Gateway spec.listeners[].hostnames, which is how the Router compares hosts (routematch.NormalizeHost) and what RFC 4343 allows. Ports and trailing dots stay as authored. It is the only normalization not driven by the schema: the two fields are identified by $defs name because no marker exists.

Normalize sorts the members of every object in the hub tree into RFC 8785 order, not only those of open configs (02 req 18). This makes materialized trees equal regardless of authored member order (01 property P1). Canonical bytes do not change.
In 01 req 36, filterClass is materialized only for plugin. This follows R-7 and CR 19 instead: filterClass is materialized for every type, and stage G adds no filterClass check.

01 req 53 asks for a yield once 100 µs of work have passed. internal/clock is not in this package's allowed imports, so workers call runtime.Gosched between resources and every 4,096 nodes instead of using a timer.

Stage G reports duplicate list entries only when normalization creates them (for example 90s and 1m30s in one set, or A.example and a.example). Authored duplicates are stage F's (01 req 34). Stage G only runs on resources that passed stage F, so nothing is reported twice.

The typed Policy config is decoded only from the members the schema declares, so an undeclared member of an open config whose name differs from a field only in letter case (encoding/json matches names case-insensitively) cannot override that field. Policy.Spec.Config, the raw JSON, still holds every member.

Conversion-data contract for future (M3) converters: a spoke's ToHub consumes the annotation it reads, including an annotations or metadata object its FromHub created. Registry.ToHub then strips any leftover annotation and removes an annotations object that the strip leaves empty.

Finding 2: when the run hits the cap, which diagnostics are kept can depend on the worker count, as with the diag.Collector contract. Below the cap the output is unchanged and deterministic (TestRunDeterministic still passes). The RZ-CFG-001 entry has no file, so after sorting it comes first, as in diag.Collector.List().

Finding 3: one encoding/json call cannot yield inside. Decode now splits values into pieces of at most 256 nodes: struct members and map members in batches, slice elements in batches copied into place, and a large value decoded straight into its field when the member name is exactly one field's JSON name. Four kinds of value stay one unit: (a) a value whose type has its own UnmarshalJSON, now called directly with the compact JSON text, so json.RawMessage is a plain copy but JSONSchemaDocument still runs json.Valid; (b) interfaces and arrays; (c) a large member whose field is promoted, ambiguous or has a ,string tag (no v1alpha1 type has one); (d) nulls and values whose JSON type does not match their Go type. appendJSON now rejects number text outside the RFC 8259 grammar, so a directly called UnmarshalJSON always receives valid JSON.

Finding 4: TestScaleLinear compares bytes allocated, like internal/config/canonical's test. It catches per-member allocation (paths, indexes, copies) but not a per-member scan that allocates nothing, which tree.Node.Get scans are. BenchmarkScale times the same shapes for that.

Finding 6: instead of validating each default alone, the test runs stage F (schemaview.Set.Validate) on the minimal resource before and after Materialize. It requires that no new finding appears, which also catches problems reported at the parent level. A negative control proves the check detects an out-of-range or off-enum default.

remainingMinor.where: internal/config/defaults/chunk.go:39-42,63-66 (an interface target is always decoded whole) and decode.go:39-44; 01 req 53 (remainder of earlier minor finding 3)
remainingMinor.issue: Most of the time-based yield fix holds, but Decode still runs a single encoding/json call for large values at interface (any) positions. These are the member values of v1alpha1.PluginConfig (map[string]any) and of Plugin spec.configSchema (map[string]any). JSONSchemaDocument.UnmarshalJSON is a similar case: it runs json.Valid over the whole inline schema between two timer reads. I probed with go test -overlay, using an instrumented copy of work.go that records the longest gap between two check() calls; no repo files were touched. A plugin Policy config {"x": [12,000 small objects]} and a Plugin configSchema of the same size each ran about 31 ms between timer reads, inside one whole() encoding/json call. A validation.json-schema enum of 30,000 strings ran about 0.5 ms inside unmarshaler(). Typed shapes behave as intended: the 12,000-label, 12,000-endpoint Upstream had a longest gap of 0.4 ms. Two statements are therefore not true for plugin configs and configSchema: the package doc's 'Large values are decoded in pieces of at most 256 nodes', and the claim in the report that Decode is split. With a large source, one any-valued member can run for hundreds of milliseconds without yielding.
remainingMinor.fix: Split interface targets in the chunker. When the target is a nil interface and the node is a KindMap or KindList, build a map[string]any or []any directly. Decode each member or element through c.decode into a fresh any value, and set the result into the interface. Leaves give exactly what encoding/json with UseNumber gives: json.Number, string, bool, or nil. Add a plugin-config case and a Plugin configSchema case to TestChunkedDecodeSplits and TestChunkedDecodeEqualsWhole. For JSONSchemaDocument, accept the json.Valid cost and document it in the package comment and in chunker's doc. pkg/ is not WP-37's to change, so if that cost matters, raise a request against the pkg owner.

remainingMinor.issue: The switch to comparing allocated bytes removed the wall-clock dependence, but the test can no longer see the regression class its own comment names: 'a per-member Get, Select or ItemElem would make stage G quadratic'. Those scans allocate nothing. I probed with an overlay that added `_, _ = n.Get(m.Key)` per member to normalizer.visit. BenchmarkScale then reported labels at 4.6 ms for 1,500 members and 234 ms for 12,000 (51x for 8x the members); open config members and json schema document showed the same. TestScaleLinear still passed, with byte ratios of 7.7 to 8.4. As written, it guards only against per-member copies, paths and indexes.
remainingMinor.fix: Make the comment accurate: it detects per-member allocation, not scans. Back it with a measure that does not depend on the machine and that counts the stage's own lookups. For example, send the stage's per-member Get, Select and ItemElem calls through a small helper that increments a counter on work (only Run-local state, so no package-level variables), and assert that counter scales by about 8x. Alternatively, have internal/tool/benchgate enforce the BenchmarkScale n:8n ratio.

Doc 02 and stage F (schemaview) should state that null is rejected in free content and in inline or plugin JSON Schema documents in M1, or else define a representation for null. commitTitle: feat(config): add stage I precedence and effective Filter Chains
summary:
I built WP-38 in internal/config/precedence/. It is stage I of the configuration pipeline. A Resolver (New(reg, Options{Body, Files})) builds a hub.Chain for every Route. Each chain holds the client Phases plus one leg per Upstream, and lists removed Gateway Policies with replaced ones before excluded ones. The chain is built from Gateway, Route and Upstream attachments using slots, excludePolicies/replacement and overridable. Phase placement comes from registry.Phases: authz.cel uses the injected body oracle, and headers, transform.* and plugin follow their configs. Entries are ordered by class, then scope, then position. Response Phases and onChunk run in reverse; onLog keeps request order. Legs follow first appearance in spec.upstreams (by name) or composition steps (authored order).

Stage I is the only stage that raises RZ-CFG-018/019/020/038 (Resolve) and RZ-CFG-029 (CheckPolicies, once per Policy whether attached or not). Run combines both into one sorted list. Diagnostics carry file:line:column through the tree positions, or through an optional FileTable. RZ-CFG-019 points to where `overridable: false` is declared using diag.Related, so the text form reproduces the configuration model's Diagnostics example byte for byte (`routes/cart-grpc.yaml:11:7 ... (declared in policies/common.yaml:46:3)`).

Unresolved references (RZ-CFG-009) are skipped without a diagnostic. The Gateway list and each Upstream list are checked once. Phase selection runs once per (Policy, scope). Work runs on a bounded worker pool that Resolve owns and waits for, and the result does not depend on scheduling. Rows(c, b) produces the render --effective rows using the 02 req 51 reason templates and JSON member order.

Tests:
- The worked example: orders-summary rows equal the configuration model's table (12 rows).
- Text and JSON goldens for all three example Routes. The example Bundle is copied verbatim from the configuration model into testdata.
- 21 YAML fixtures covering every case of 02 test 16, each with file, line and column.
- Unit tests for Phase selection (test 17), ordering (test 18), replace/exclude, slots per scope, the cache guardrail, programming errors, locator fallbacks, the worker pool, determinism and concurrent use.
- FuzzPrecedenceInvariants (02 test 30, precedence laws).
- BenchmarkResolve over 5,000 Routes.
- A scale test with 3,000-member lists.

contractRequests: Architecture 1.2 row for config/precedence: add config/tree and pkg/config/v1alpha1 to 'May import'. The package reads typed Gateway, Route, Upstream, Policy and Plugin objects. It also takes an optional *tree.FileTable (Options.Files) and reads tree positions and tree.StyleDefaulted for diagnostic locations. `expr` can be dropped from the row: the injected oracle is typed registry.BodyOracle, which expr.Compiler satisfies (asserted in TestCompilerIsBodyOracle).

Spec 02 section 3 precedence API differs from what was built; please re-sync the text. Built: New(reg *registry.Registry, Options{Body registry.BodyOracle; Files *tree.FileTable}). Resolve(ctx, *hub.Bundle, workers) (map[string]*hub.Chain, diag.List, error), whose error covers ctx.Err(), registry.ErrNoBodyOracle, ErrUnknownType and a config of the wrong type. CheckPolicies(*hub.Bundle) diag.List. Run(ctx, b, workers), which combines both into one sorted list. Rows is a package function, Rows(c *hub.Chain, b *hub.Bundle) []Row, because hub.Chain is a WP-01 type and cannot take a method. Row has fields Phase, Leg, Policy, Type, FilterClass, Slot, From, Reason with JSON tags in the 02 req 52 order.

WP-69 (pipeline facade): build the Resolver with Options{Body: the expr.Compiler, Files: the loader's FileTable} and call Run at stage I. Without Files, positions fall back to hub.Resource.Source.File for nodes in the resource's own file, and to the resource start for overlay-added nodes.
WP-58 (render): Rows(chain, bundle) gives the --effective rows. The removed rows take their type and filterClass from the Bundle's materialized Policy, so render needs no registry.

docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md (WP-29/WP-31 owners): the RZ-CFG-038 message has no documented wording. The proposed text, pinned by goldens, is: 'Response Cache Policy "" is combined with Policy "

" (, Filter class ), which runs in onRequestBody: a cache hit would skip it'. The RZ-CFG-019 replace wording (02 req 35.2, proposed) is implemented as written. Its 'declared in' location is a diag.Related entry, which the text form prints exactly as in the CM example.
deviations: Imports internal/config/tree and pkg/config/v1alpha1, which are not in the 1.2 row, and does not import internal/expr (see contract requests). No lint rule is affected.
Resolve returns a third value, an error, for programming errors and context cancellation. Spec 02 section 3 lists only (chains, diags).

02 req 2 and 40 are read as: skip each unresolved reference (a missing Policy, Plugin or Upstream) silently and still compute the Route's chain from the references that did resolve. The Route is not dropped. Diagnostics stay exact and every other error is still reported in one run. The pipeline stops after stage H errors, so these partial chains never reach a Validated result.

Cascade control (no rule in the specs): an entry rejected with RZ-CFG-020, the second entry of a slot (RZ-CFG-018), or a Route Policy whose replacement of a locked Gateway Policy is refused (RZ-CFG-019) is left out of the chain. A locked Gateway Policy stays in the chain after RZ-CFG-019. One mistake therefore yields one finding.
Leg order sorts spec.upstreams by name itself. On stage-G output this has no effect, because map sorting already did it. It keeps 02 req 41 true for callers that pass unnormalized typed objects.

Tests parse YAML fixtures through internal/config/profile, using only its exported Parse and FormatYAML, as the S1 note allows. Typed objects are built by JSON-decoding tree.JSONValue(), because WP-37's defaults/convert packages are not committed. If WP-33's parser changes, fixture positions are the first thing to recheck.

remainingMinor.where: internal/config/precedence/precedence.go:62-63, locate.go:9, resolve.go:17, rows.go:13 (architecture 1.2 row for config/precedence)
remainingMinor.issue: The package imports internal/config/tree (for Options.Files and to walk hub.Resource.Tree) and pkg/config/v1alpha1. Neither is in its 1.2 'May import' list, which names config/hub, config/registry, config/diag, phase and expr. Both are lower layers and create no cycle, and depguard does not enforce the row, so lint passes. It still breaks the rule that a package imports 'only those its row in 1.2 lists'.
remainingMinor.fix: Send a contract change request to add config/tree and v1alpha1 to the config/precedence row in 1.2 (the package cannot avoid either: hub.Object returns *v1alpha1 types and hub.Resource.Tree is a *tree.Node). Mention it in the WP report.

remainingMinor.issue: Resolve calls Options.Body.ReferencesRequestBody from several worker goroutines (selectAll on the forEach pool), but the Options doc never says the oracle must be safe for concurrent use. expr.Compiler is documented as safe, so production callers are fine. A custom oracle, such as a test stub or a future wrapper, that is not safe would race without any warning.
remainingMinor.fix: Add to the Options.Body doc: 'Body must be safe for concurrent use: Resolve calls it from up to workers goroutines.'

remainingMinor.issue: Rows builds its own registry.New() to find the Filter class of a removed Policy that has no materialized filterClass. It ignores the registry the Resolver was built with, so a Resolver made with a non-default registry could print a different class for removed rows than for live entries. After stage G this path is effectively dead, because filterClass is always materialized.
remainingMinor.fix: Use only the materialized p.Spec.FilterClass and leave FilterClass empty otherwise, or make Rows a method on *Resolver (or pass the registry in) so live and removed rows use one registry.

remainingMinor.issue: TestScale uses time.Now and time.Since. They only feed t.Logf, but architecture section 0 item 4 says time.Now appears only in clock.Real, and tests must not depend on wall-clock time. The test also claims the run 'stays linear' without asserting it.
remainingMinor.fix: Remove the timing log, or use b.Elapsed in a benchmark. If linearity matters, assert an allocation or operation count instead of time.

remainingMinor.issue: BenchmarkResolve's Bundle has no positioned trees and no FileTable, so the locator path is never measured. In the pipeline, the per-entry tree walk and the FileTable mutex taken on every Location call (tree.FileTable.Location locks t.mu) run for every attachment. The 5,000-Route figure (about 35 ms/op) therefore understates the real stage I cost and hides lock contention between workers.
remainingMinor.fix: Give the benchmark Bundle Gateway, Route and Upstream trees (as listTree does in scale_test.go) and pass a FileTable in Options, so the 02 section 6 benchmark covers the production path.

remainingMinor.issue: The property checks soundness only: a locked Policy is never removed, and no RZ-CFG-019 is raised for excluding an overridable Policy. It does not check completeness: that every exclusion or same-slot replacement of an attached overridable:false Gateway Policy raises RZ-CFG-019. It also never checks the one-Policy-per-slot law on each Upstream leg, only on the client leg. If either broke, for example 019 being dropped on replace, the fuzz target would not catch it (the unit tests and fixtures still would).
remainingMinor.fix: For each Route, compute the attached locked Gateway Policies and assert one RZ-CFG-019 for every excludePolicies entry naming one and for every resolved, scope-valid Route entry in its slot. Run the same slot-uniqueness check over every c.Legs[i].Phases.
